analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/developer/build.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and edits CI caching prose: the Darkbloom Sandbox cache note (head ~573-576), a new Darkbloom cache paragraph (head ~658-680) and edits near head 724-730 and 757. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the later head text, including the 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step that sets CI_ACTIONS..., was not fully visible. The supplied evidence is base text plus a partial patch.

I saw no code, workflow, key, crypto or protocol changes. The documentation describes CI cache routing: DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL on the guest loopback, with Actions cache steps skipped when the plane provides no Darkbloom cache. It also records an earlier leak of a master-push build cache to GitHub's refs/heads/master scope from a Darkbloom host. That is a CI/supply-chain concern, and it is outside the provider threat model's assets and boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, T-041 etc.). It is not a runtime provider change, and none of the canonical threats (e.g. T-041 prefix-cache SSD storage) are affected.

Supply-chain risk from cache poisoning in release builds remains separate. The base text already states that CI (master) restores only the strict tier and that release lanes are separate. Whether the actual workflow changes elsewhere in the PR preserve those isolation properties is not verifiable from this documentation-only unit. If the PR changes .github actions or workflows, the integration pass should review them: a Darkbloom-cache-served restore into release or signing lanes, and the cache key scoping. No finding is made here because no such code was supplied.
